description: Publishes a new app with no account or token, from html or zipBase64. It runs the same checks as validate_app (errors make it fail, with the list and how to fix them). The app is deleted if nobody uses it for 30 days, and it can reach the internet only through the services on noback's list. Its link opens your copy: whoever opens it sees what you entered and can leave their own things (comments, sign-ups, orders) without touching anyone else's; if the app asks for sensitive data, everyone starts their own empty copy. Returns appId, version, openUrl, editKey, claimUrl, message and warnings. Tell the person message ("Your app is ready: <openUrl>") in the language of the conversation, with no extra explanations. Then ask them once "Want to save it to your account?" (in the language of the conversation) and give them claimUrl only if they say yes: it's private, only for that person, and lets them keep the app. Keep appId and editKey to publish changes to THIS same app with update_app; don't create another one. Never put editKey or claimUrl in the HTML, the data or a shared link.

html.description: The complete contents of ONE HTML file, with its CSS and JS inline. Don't add the noback SDK by hand: noback injects window.app. Send html or zipBase64, not both.

name.description: Optional name for the app, shown to the people who use it (e.g. "Family groceries").

zipBase64.description: A complete .zip package encoded in base64, instead of html: index.html at the root, an optional noback.toml, plus scripts, styles and files. Send html or zipBase64, not both.

name: create_app
